  7. the demo shows a BASIC session: "READY", "10 PRINT "HELLO"", "RUN", "HELLO"
- motion: character-by-character printing with the jolt; line advance; the demo session
- states to show: a BASIC session mid-print; a faded ribbon; at scale 0.75 with a longer viewport
- priority: A

### G16.2 · Epson MX-80 9-pin dot-matrix on tractor-feed paper
- slug: `print-epson-mx80-tractor`
- element: `sk-print-epson-mx80`
- kind: output
- value: text stream — `print(str)` at 80 chars/s with bidirectional head passes; `mode` = "draft" | "nlq" (double-strike); `paper` = "white" | "greenbar"; the perforated tractor strips are always drawn
- machine: Epson MX-80 (1980) / FX-80 (1983) 9-pin dot-matrix printer output on continuous tractor-feed paper with the tear-off perforated edge strips
- era: 1980s
- origin: Japan
- size: 9.5″ paper (with tractor strips) → build at 400 × 300 px viewport, the paper wider than the text area
- materials: continuous paper with a perforated tractor strip each side (a row of round holes, the perforation a dotted line); optionally green-bar ruled; each character built from 9-pin dots, the dots slightly elongated horizontally and overlapping in NLQ; a black ribbon that fades to grey-brown; a horizontal fold line every 11″ (a slightly darker crease across the page)
- palette: paper #f4f1e8, green-bar #cfe3cf bands, ribbon ink #262320 draft / #1a1815 NLQ, faded #5a5048, hole rim #d8d3c6 with a #b9b3a4 shadow, perforation #b0aa9a, crease #e4e0d4
- typeface: none — a 9-pin draft glyph table (the Epson ROM shapes: 9 × 9 draft cells with the characteristic descenders using the bottom two pins, a slashed zero), dots 1.6 × 1.2 px ellipses on a 1.5 px pitch; NLQ draws each glyph twice with a 0.6 px offset
- the tells:
  1. characters visibly made of dots — in draft the dots are distinct with gaps; in NLQ they merge into a smeared, heavier stroke (the double-strike)
  2. tractor strips with round holes every 12.7 mm and the dotted perforation line, and the paper's fold crease every 66 lines
  3. the head passes: lines print left-to-right then right-to-left (a moving 3 px darker rectangle sweeps the line as it appears)
  4. green-bar mode: alternating three-line pale-green bands with a fine rule
  5. ribbon fade: the ink drifts toward grey-brown along the page as `ribbon` decreases, and one column of dots is faintly missing (a bent pin, seeded)
  6. the demo prints a program listing with line numbers and a "READY." prompt, then a banner line of "#" characters
- motion: the head sweep at 80 chars/s; line feeds at 40 ms; `demo(t)` prints a listing
- states to show: draft on white; NLQ on green-bar; faded ribbon at scale 0.7
- priority: B

### G16.3 · Thermal receipt with the serrated tear
- slug: `print-thermal-receipt-tm88`
- element: `sk-print-thermal-receipt`
- kind: output
- value: text stream — `print(str)` at 150 mm/s; `columns` 42; `barcode` optional (a CODE-39-like bar pattern drawn from the digits); `cut()` tears the receipt and starts a new one
- machine: Epson TM-T88 / Star TSP thermal receipt printer output on 80 mm thermal paper, 1997–present
- era: 1990s
- origin: Japan
- size: 80 mm paper, a viewport of ~ 120 mm → build at 240 × 360 px with the paper emerging from a dark slot at the top and the serrated tear at the bottom
- materials: bright-white thermal paper with a faint blue-grey cast; slightly grey-black dot-matrix print with a soft edge (thermal dots bleed a little); a bold double-height "TOTAL" line; a barcode; a serrated (triangular) tear edge; the paper shows a faint vertical roller line and, when `sunfaded`, a yellowed band with the print going grey
- palette: paper #fbfbf9 with cast #eef0f2, print #2a2a2a with bleed #2a2a2a at 20 % (0.5 px), bold #1c1c1c, roller line #ececea, sun-faded band #efe6c4 with print #7a7a76, slot #1a1a1a
- typeface: none for the print — a 12×24 thermal glyph table (the ESC/POS font A: a plain sans with a slashed zero off); dots 1 px square on a 1 px pitch with a 0.5 px blur; "TOTAL" in double-width/double-height
- the tells:
  1. very white paper, soft grey-black print with a faint bleed — never crisp, never dark
  2. the serrated tear at the bottom: a zigzag edge of 3 px triangles, the paper's end slightly curled (a gradient)
  3. the print appears line by line very fast (150 mm/s ≈ a 24-px line every 40 ms) and the paper feeds out of a dark slot at the top
  4. the receipt layout: a centred header, item lines with right-aligned prices, a double-height TOTAL, a barcode block and a "THANK YOU" line (all generic)
  5. the paper has a faint roller line and a slight lengthwise curl shadow at the edges
  6. `sunfaded` shows a yellowed band where the print has gone grey
- motion: line-by-line at printer speed; `cut()` tears with a 200 ms edge animation and the receipt drops 20 px
- states to show: a full receipt with barcode; mid-print; sun-faded at scale 0.8
- priority: C

## G17 · Ticker-tape / punched tape

### G17.1 · Eight-level ASCII punched paper tape with sprocket holes
- slug: `tape-punched-8-level-ascii`
- element: `sk-tape-punched-8-level`
- kind: output
- value: text — punched as ASCII (8-level, even parity in the 8th hole by default) into a strip; `levels` 8 or 5 (Baudot / ITA2 for the narrower tape); `feed` px/s animates the tape passing a reader window; `colour` = "buff" | "yellow" | "pink" | "black-mylar"
- machine: the 1″ eight-level paper tape of a Teletype ASR-33 / DEC PC05 reader (ASCII), and the 11/16″ five-level tape of a Teletype Model 28 / Creed 6S (Baudot), 1930s–1970s
- era: 1960s
- origin: USA / UK
- size: 1″ (25.4 mm) tape, holes 1.83 mm on a 2.54 mm pitch → build at ×2.4, a 400 × 64 px strip (5-level: 400 × 42 px) with an optional reader window
- materials: an oiled buff paper strip with a slight translucency and a fibrous edge; round data holes (a clean punch with a tiny paper-fibre fringe) in 8 rows across the tape, and a row of smaller sprocket feed holes off-centre (between rows 3 and 4); a chad or two stuck to the surface; a fanfold crease every 8″; a hand-written leader in marker on the demo tape
- palette: buff #d9c9a0 with fibre #c9b78a at 8 % and oil translucency #fff at 10 %, yellow #e8d76a, pink #efc6c0, mylar #1a1a1a with #333 sheen; holes #1c1a16 (the dark behind the tape) with a 0.5 px #f2ead0 fringe, sprocket holes the same at 55 % diameter, crease #c2b28a, marker #1c2a5a
- typeface: none for the punches; the optional printed character row along the tape edge (some readers interpret) and the marker leader in Google "Special Elite" 400 at 12 px, and a 5 px caps ruler for the level numbers ("8 7 6 5 · 4 3 2 1")
- the tells:
  1. the sprocket row is off-centre: eight data rows with the small feed holes between rows 3 and 4 (counting from one edge) — the single detail that makes it read as real tape
  2. holes are round with a faint fibre fringe, and they show the dark background through them; the tape itself is faintly translucent so the holes' shadows are visible on the surface
  3. the tape feeds through a reader window (a black frame with a star-wheel notch) at `feed` px/s and the demo runs a loop of "HELLO WORLD" with a leader of all-holes (rubouts) and blank leader
  4. a fanfold crease as a slightly darker vertical line every 8″ with a 1 px lighter edge
  5. one or two chad discs lying on the tape (tiny buff circles with a shadow), and the marker-written leader "BIN LOADER" on the blank section
  6. the 5-level Baudot variant is narrower with the sprocket row between rows 2 and 3 and uses the ITA2 letters/figures shifts (the demo shows a "LTRS" shift hole pattern)
  7. black Mylar mode: a glossy dark tape with the holes reading as pale grey
- motion: the feed at a constant rate with a 1 px lateral wobble; `punch(str)` appends holes with a 12 ms per-character punch animation (holes pop in with a small chad flying off)
- states to show: "HELLO WORLD" 8-level buff feeding; 5-level yellow static; black Mylar at scale 0.8
- priority: A

### G17.2 · Stock ticker under a glass dome with tape spooling out
- slug: `ticker-edison-glass-dome`
- element: `sk-ticker-glass-dome`
- kind: output
- value: text stream — `print(str)` types onto ¾″ tape at 3 chars/s in the typewheel face ("T 45½ · XYZ 102¼"); the tape emerges under the dome's edge and coils; `value` holds the last 40 characters
- machine: Edison Universal Stock Ticker (1869) / Western Union self-winding ticker under a glass bell jar on a wooden base, 1870s–1960s
- era: 1900s
- origin: USA
- size: a 14″-tall dome on a 9″ base → build at 300 × 400 px including the coiling tape below
- materials: a clear glass bell jar with a brass finial, showing refraction highlights; inside, a brass mechanism with two typewheels (letters and figures) on a vertical shaft, a paper reel and a small motor; a turned mahogany base with a brass slot at the front where the tape exits; the tape is a narrow off-white strip printed in a crisp small serif; it curls and coils on the "desk" below
- palette: glass edge #dfe6ea at 50 % with #fff highlights, glass tint #cfd8dc at 6 %, brass #c9a24c → #7d5f26 with #f2dc9a glints, mahogany #5a2f1a → #7a4426, tape #f1ead6 with print #1a1814, shadow under the dome #000 at 25 %
- typeface: the typewheel face is a small crisp serif with fractions → Google "Courier Prime" 400 at 11 px for the tape text, with "½ ¼ ⅛" glyphs; the brass maker's plate in "Libre Franklin" 600 caps 5 px (generic wording)
- the tells:
  1. the dome: a tall glass bell with two vertical refraction highlights and a brass finial on top; the brass mechanism inside is seen through it with slight distortion (a 1 % barrel on the inner drawing)
  2. the typewheel turns to each letter before printing — the wheel visibly rotates (a 0–360° spin of a small lettered disc) and a hammer taps the tape, at ~3 chars/s
  3. the tape exits a brass slot at the base and coils on the surface below in loose loops (an SVG path that grows as text is printed; the loops re-flow to keep the latest 40 characters readable near the slot)
  4. the print is tiny, crisp, and includes stock-style fractions and abbreviations with the price a space away from the symbol
  5. the mahogany base with a turned edge and a brass plate; a shadow ring under the dome
  6. a small paper reel inside the dome visibly shrinking over a long demo run
- motion: the wheel spin per character, the hammer tap, the tape growth; `demo(t)` prints a stream of generic symbols and prices
- states to show: mid-print with a coil of tape; a long coil after many characters; at scale 0.6
- priority: B

### G17.3 · Piano roll passing over a tracker bar
- slug: `tape-piano-roll-tracker-bar`
- element: `sk-tape-piano-roll`
- kind: output
- value: bits — a stream of 88-lane note events (`notes` JSON array of {lane, start, length}) rendered as slots in a wide paper roll that scrolls down over a brass tracker bar; `tempo` sets the roll speed; `lyrics` optional text in the margin (a "word roll")
- machine: Aeolian / QRS / Welte-Mignon player-piano roll on the tracker bar of an upright player, 1900s–1930s
- era: 1910s
- origin: USA
- size: 11¼″ roll over a tracker bar → build at 360 × 280 px showing the roll from the take-up spool down to the bar, the bar itself and the two spool chucks
- materials: a wide cream paper roll with a faint horizontal grain, printed with a light red or green guide line and a small perforation legend at the edge; long rectangular slots and short holes (the notes) punched cleanly; a brass tracker bar with 88 small holes in a row (dark, with brass rims) that the paper slides over; a wooden spool box with two turned chucks and a tension bar; lyrics printed in blue-black at the right margin on word rolls
- palette: paper #efe5cc with grain #e2d6b8 at 6 %, guide line #c8544a at 40 %, slots #2a241e (the dark bar behind), brass bar #c9a24c → #8a6a2a with hole rims #e2c878 and hole interiors #1c1814, wood #5a3a22 → #7a5233, lyrics #2b3a66
- typeface: the roll's printed legend and lyrics → Google "Special Elite" 400 at 11 px for lyrics and "Libre Franklin" 500 caps 5 px for the edge legend ("TEMPO 70")
- the tells:
  1. the roll moves down over the bar: slots and holes scroll toward the tracker bar and a slot becomes "live" when its bottom edge crosses the bar's hole row — the corresponding hole on the bar glows faintly darker and a tiny key indicator strip beneath the bar dips
  2. the tracker bar: a brass strip with 88 evenly spaced small holes, each with a bright rim, and two larger holes at the ends for the expression tracks
  3. the paper is slightly transparent where it passes over the bar (the bar's holes show through as dark dots), and it curves onto the take-up spool at the bottom with a roll-curvature shadow
  4. long sustained notes are long slots, chords are aligned rows of short holes — the punch pattern reads as music
  5. the lyrics scroll with the paper in the right margin, upside-down-free and set in a typewriter face, a word per line
  6. the spool chucks turn (a rotating hub texture) at a rate matching the roll, and the take-up spool's diameter grows slowly over a long demo
- motion: continuous scroll at `tempo`; live-note flash on crossing; hub rotation; `demo(t)` plays a generic ragtime-ish pattern
- states to show: playing mid-roll with lyrics; paused with a chord over the bar; at scale 0.6 full-width
- priority: C

# H · Lamps and light, I · Mechanical and fluid, J · Panels and furniture

*Phase 3 of `../PLAN.md`, built on `p2-HIJ.md`. One entry per style, exactly one priority-A per code. Conventions: for lit legends (H7) `value: boolean` means "lit" and the `label` attribute carries the legend text. For section J the element is a swatch or a piece of furniture that other pages mount things on — `kind: output`, `value: text` is the legend printed on it (may be empty) or `boolean` where the piece has a state. Sizes are natural CSS px at `scale="1"`. Seven-segment digits, beam-drawn readouts and stencil bridges are SVG paths, never a font. Machine names are for reference; builds use generic wordmarks.*

---

## H1 · Pilot lamp with jewel lens

### H1.1 · Fender blackface red jewel in a fluted chrome bezel
- slug: `pilot-jewel-fender-blackface`
- element: `sk-pilot-jewel-fender`
- kind: output
- value: boolean (lit); attribute `color` = red | amber | blue | green (red is the reference)
- machine: Fender Deluxe Reverb / Twin Reverb / Bassman blackface and silverface amps — the ~1" faceted jewel pilot over a #47 bayonet bulb
- era: 1960s
- origin: USA
- size: jewel Ø 25 mm in a Ø 32 mm bezel standing ~10 mm proud → build at 64 × 64 px natural (bezel Ø 56, jewel Ø 44); optional legend strip below adds 16 px
- materials: chrome-plated brass bezel with 24 radial flutes; dome-cut faceted red acrylic jewel (~24 facets in three rings), slightly yellowed and micro-crazed; #47 lamp behind, its glass and filament visible through the jewel when off; black textured panel behind
- palette: bezel chrome #f6f6f6 → #a8a8a8 → #303030 with a dark horizon band; jewel unlit #5c0f10, facet edges #8a2020; jewel lit core #ff3b22, facet highlights #ffb4a0, panel halo rgba(255,70,40,.35) 10 px; filament unlit #6d4a3b, bulb glass glint #c9c2b8; panel #141414
- typeface: none on the lamp; if a legend is shown, blackface caps in a Futura-like → Josefin Sans 600, 8 px, tracking 0.12em, #e8e4d8
- the tells:
  1. the dome is cut in facets — an outer ring of 8 trapezoids, a middle ring of 8, a centre of 8 — each a flat plane with its own highlight, so lit it reads as a starburst, not a smooth glow
  2. unlit, the jewel is deep wine-red and you can see the bulb inside: pale glass and a little hairpin filament, slightly off-centre
  3. the bezel is fluted radially and stands well proud, casting a crescent shadow down-right onto the panel
  4. lit, the brightest point is where the filament is — low and off-centre, never in the middle of the dome; the upper facets run a shade cooler and dimmer
  5. light spills onto the neighbouring bezel flutes (they pick up a pink tint) and throws a soft red halo on the panel
  6. the acrylic is yellowed and crazed — two or three hairline cracks catch the light on the outer facets
  7. one specular white glint at 11 o'clock on the dome, present lit and unlit
- motion: incandescent — brightness rises over ~140 ms ease-out, decays over ~320 ms going orange before dark; `flicker` adds a 2 % shimmer at ~8 Hz for a tired lamp
- states to show: off (filament visible); on; amber variant on; half-brightness standby
- priority: A

### H1.2 · Dialight ¾" jewel with a knurled nickel ring on grey wrinkle
- slug: `pilot-jewel-dialight-knurled`
- element: `sk-pilot-jewel-dialight`
- kind: output
- value: boolean (lit); attribute `color` = red | green | amber | white | blue; attribute `test` lights it regardless (push-to-test)
- machine: Dialight 081 / 095-series panel indicator — T-3¼ bayonet lamp under a screw-in domed cut-glass lens, on US industrial, military and test panels
- era: 1950s
- origin: USA
- size: lens Ø 19 mm, bezel Ø 26 mm → build at 48 × 48 px natural; the demo is a row of five mixed colours, 288 × 48
- materials: polished nickel bezel with a knurled outer ring (~48 fine teeth) and a flat inner lip; shallow domed lens with ~40 small diamond facets in glass-clear coloured acrylic; set in grey wrinkle-painted steel with a hex nut behind
- palette: nickel #ececec → #9b9b9b → #454545 with a warm cast #e9e6dc; red off #4d0e0e / on #ff2d1e; green off #0d3d24 / on #35ff7a; amber off #4e2f07 / on #ffb020; white off #8a8a84 / on #fff7e0; blue off #0f2650 / on #4a8cff; wrinkle panel #6e7378 with web #5a5f64
- typeface: legend engraved below, white-filled monoline caps → Barlow 500, 7 px, tracking 0.1em, #e6e6e6
- the tells:
  1. the knurl — a ring of tiny alternating light/dark teeth around the bezel — is the Dialight signature
  2. a row of identical bezels with different lens colours side by side: the lenses are interchangeable
  3. the facets are small and many (a grid of little diamonds) so the lit lens sparkles rather than flares
  4. the dome is shallow — a low cap, not a hemisphere — with one long highlight across the top
  5. off, the lens is a deep saturated glass colour, not black; the lamp shows as a paler ellipse behind
  6. the wrinkle paint around it has a fine raised web catching light on its ridges
  7. the bezel lip casts a hard inner shadow on the lens at top-left
- motion: incandescent rise ~120 ms, fall ~280 ms; `test` lights the whole row for as long as it is set
- states to show: a row of five all off; red and green lit; all lit (lamp test)
- priority: B

### H1.3 · Soviet ribbed-lens СЕТЬ lamp on black carbolite
- slug: `pilot-jewel-soviet-set-ribbed`
- element: `sk-pilot-jewel-soviet-set`

- origin: USA

- materials: black-painted aluminium glareshield with a matte black bezel; dead-face caps — black opaque face with the legend engraved through so only the letters light; amber lamps behind the six-pack and MASTER CAUTION, red behind FIRE WARN; the two square caps are pushbuttons with a hairline gap around them
- palette: bezel #15161a; cap face #232428 with a #0e0f11 edge; unlit legend just visible as #2e2f33; lit amber legend #ffb324 with bloom rgba(255,179,36,.35) 6 px; lit red legend #ff3a2e with bloom rgba(255,58,46,.4); glareshield around #1a1a1c with a faint 45° brushed sheen
- typeface: engraved caps in Boeing's Futura-like placard face → Josefin Sans 600, 7.5 px, tracking 0.1em, two lines centred; the square caps carry "MASTER / CAUTION" and "FIRE / WARN" at 9 px
- the tells:
  1. dead-face: unlit, the caps are near-black and the legends almost invisible — a barely-there grey ghost of the letters
  2. only the letters light, not the tile; the face stays black around glowing amber text
  3. the six-pack is two columns of three with the legends in a fixed order; OVHT/DET wraps to two lines
  4. the two big square caps sit apart from the six-pack with a hairline gap around them (they are buttons); pressing MASTER CAUTION extinguishes it and the six-pack recalls
  5. lit letters bloom slightly beyond their strokes and tint the black face around them
  6. FIRE WARN is the one red thing on a panel of amber
  7. the glareshield is matte black with a faint diagonal sheen, no screws visible — the caps are retained from behind
  8. a slight brightness gradient across each cap (the lamp is at one end)
- motion: lamp rise ~120 ms, fall ~250 ms; a new caution lights MASTER CAUTION and the relevant tile together; `activate` on MASTER CAUTION clears it (the tile stays); FIRE WARN can `flash` at 1 Hz with the fire bell implied
- states to show: all dark; FUEL + MASTER CAUTION lit; FIRE WARN flashing with ELEC and APU lit; the recall state (all six lit)
- priority: A

### H3.3 · Panalarm industrial annunciator window grid with first-out sequence
- slug: `annunciator-panalarm-window-grid`

- machine: Panalarm 90-series / Ronan X11 modular annunciator as fitted in nuclear, chemical and power-station control rooms (TMI-2, Westinghouse plants) — the grey bezel with a grid of white windows
- era: 1970s
- origin: USA
- size: windows 2" × 3" in a bezel → build at 460 × 250 px natural (windows 72 × 48 with 3 px mullions; 26 px button row below)
- materials: grey enamelled steel bezel with a thin aluminium mullion grid; each window a white translucent acrylic with a black film legend; two lamps behind each; four square black pushbuttons with white legends below
- palette: bezel #8e9296 (telephone grey) with edge #6c7074; mullions #b9bcbf; window unlit #d6d4cc (a dull white, slightly grey-yellow); lit white #fffbe8 with a warm centre #fff2c0; lit amber variant #ffc44a; lit red #ff5a48; legend #111111; buttons #1c1c1c with legends #f2f2f2

  3. an unacknowledged alarm flashes fast; ACK makes it steady; when the condition clears it flashes slow until RESET
  4. the first-out window (the first alarm of a cascade) flashes at a different rate from the others
  5. the light behind a window is uneven — two lamps make two soft hot spots
  6. the button row: four square black buttons with white caps, ACK worn shiny
  7. an engraved panel number plate at the bezel corner
- motion: alarm flash 2 Hz (50 %); first-out flash 4 Hz; return-to-normal slow flash 0.5 Hz; steady after ACK; RESET clears rtn windows; TEST lights all

- era: 1980s
- origin: Japan

- palette: panel #17181a; window #0d0e10 with a 1 px #2b2c30 bevel; green unlit #0f2a17 / lit #3dff73; amber unlit #3a2705 / lit #ffb524; red unlit #3a0d0c / lit #ff2f26; each lit LED blooms rgba(colour,.35) 3 px; scale #e9e7df

- machine: the Soviet ИН-13 linear neon indicator tube (Океан radios, hobby clocks and VU meters) — a long glass tube with a continuous orange neon column
- era: 1970s
- origin: USSR
- size: tube ~ 120 × 10 mm → build at 32 × 300 px natural (tube 18 px wide, vertical, with a printed scale to its right)
- materials: clear glass tube with a flattened end, a long cathode strip inside, an auxiliary cathode dot at the base; mounted on two black clips against a grey hammertone panel; scale on a paper card beside
- palette: glass #2a2a2e with edge glints #9a9aa2; column lit #ff7a1c core → #ffb066 edge with a rgba(255,122,28,.5) 6 px glow, the very top of the column a paler #ffd2a0; auxiliary dot #ff8d3c always lit; unlit strip #3b2b22; panel #6f7d6c hammertone; scale card #e9e3d2 with #222 ticks
- typeface: scale 0…10 in a heavy Cyrillic-era grotesk → Noto Sans 700, 6 px
- the tells:
  1. a continuous column, not segments — the glow rises smoothly like a thermometer of fire
  2. the top of the column is soft and slightly brighter, and it flickers a hair as it moves
  3. a permanent tiny glowing dot at the base (the keep-alive cathode)
  4. the glass shows two long highlight lines and the metal strip inside as a dark bar behind the glow
  5. the column tints the glass and the panel orange around it
  6. a paper scale beside it, slightly askew, with Cyrillic numerals
- motion: column follows the value with ~120 ms lag and a 1 px random jitter at the tip; strike from zero begins at the base and runs up
- states to show: zero (dot only); half; near full with the tip flickering
- priority: C

## H12 · CRT phosphor / oscilloscope trace

### H12.1 · Tektronix 465 — internal graticule, P31 green, bloom and persistence
- slug: `crt-tektronix-465`
- element: `sk-crt-tek-465`
- kind: output
- value: waveform count 500 (samples 0…1 across ten divisions; attribute `value2` for channel 2; `intensity` 0…1, `focus` 0…1, `illum` 0…1 graticule illumination)
- machine: Tektronix 465 / 475 portable oscilloscope — the 8 × 10 division internal-graticule CRT with a green light filter in a black bezel on the cream-and-blue-grey front
- era: 1970s
- origin: USA
- size: graticule 8 × 10 cm on the tube face; the bezel ~ 125 × 110 mm → build at 360 × 300 px natural (screen 320 × 256, 32 px per division; bezel 20 px)
- materials: black plastic bezel with a camera-mount ring and four corner screw holes; a green tinted acrylic filter over a flat-faced rectangular CRT with the graticule etched inside the faceplate; the tube's glass slightly grey-green; the 465's cream panel visible around the bezel
- palette: bezel #1f1f21 with a rim highlight #3b3b3f; screen off #141c17 with a faint darker vignette at the corners; graticule lines #5c8a6a at 45 % (illuminated up to #a4d4b4 by `illum`); centre-line hash marks the same; trace core #6cff8c with an inner #d8ffe0 where the beam moves slowly, bloom rgba(108,255,140,.35) 3 px, persistence tail #2c6b3c; panel #e6e1cf with blue-grey #5c6f80 legends
- typeface: bezel legends none; the panel corners show "INTENSITY" / "FOCUS" / "BEAM FIND" in Tek's Helvetica-based caps → Inter 500, 6.5 px, #2a2f36 (decorative, optional)
- the tells:
  1. the internal graticule: lines are in the same plane as the trace, so there is no parallax and the trace sits exactly on them; the lines are dim etched grey-green, never white
  2. the centre vertical and horizontal lines carry small hash marks every 0.2 division; the 0 % / 10 % / 90 % / 100 % dashed rise-time lines run across near the top and bottom
  3. the P31 green: a yellowish green with a bright core; where the beam moves fast (a rising edge) the trace is thin and dim, where it moves slowly (a flat top) it is fat and bright
  4. bloom: a soft glow around the trace that widens with `intensity`; over-driven it blurs and the graticule washes
  5. persistence: a short trailing fade (~80 ms) behind a moving waveform, so a changing signal leaves a faint ghost
  6. the screen goes a shade darker at the corners; the filter is green-tinted so "black" is dark green
  7. retrace is blanked — the beam never draws its way back; a stopped sweep leaves one bright dot
  8. a small "1" and "2" channel identifier at the left edge of each trace (as a beam-drawn glyph)
- motion: a sweep animation at `timebase` ms per division (default 2 ms → the whole width in 20 ms, i.e. continuous); trace redraw each frame with a 4-frame decaying history layer; `intensity` 0 blanks; `focus` < 1 blurs 1–3 px
- states to show: a 1 kHz sine, two channels; a square wave with overshoot and bright flat tops; a stopped sweep (single dot); graticule illumination on
- priority: A

### H12.2 · Tektronix 2465 with beam-drawn on-screen readout
- slug: `crt-tektronix-2465-readout`
- element: `sk-crt-tek-2465`
- kind: output

- machine: Tektronix 2465 / 2445 / 2235 — the 300 MHz four-channel portable whose CRT writes alphanumeric readout at the top and bottom of the screen with the same beam

- palette: screen off #131a18; graticule #587f66; trace #7cff9a with bloom; readout glyphs #9dffb2, a touch dimmer than the trace, with the same bloom; bezel #232326

## H13 · Radar PPI

### H13.1 · Decca hooded marine PPI with EBL cursor and two-colour long-persistence afterglow
- slug: `radar-ppi-decca-marine`
- element: `sk-radar-ppi-decca`
- kind: output
- value: waveform count 360 (nearest echo range 0…1 per degree of bearing, drawn as the coast/land return); attribute `targets` = "bearing,range,size;…" for point echoes; `ebl` deg, `vrm` 0…1, `rpm` default 24, `range-rings` default 4
- machine: Decca RM 916 / Decca 101 marine radar display — a large round hooded tube in a grey pedestal console with a rotating sweep, range rings, a heading marker, an electronic bearing line, and a long-persistence phosphor that flashes blue and fades yellow-green
- era: 1960s
- origin: UK
- size: 12" tube → build at 360 × 360 px natural (screen Ø 320 inside a 20 px black hood ring)
- materials: a round CRT behind a black rubber viewing hood (rendered as a heavy dark vignette ring with a soft inner edge); a bearing scale ring engraved 0–360 around the screen in white on black; a grey hammertone console just visible outside the hood
- palette: screen #0a0c0b; sweep line #cfe6ff (blue-white) with bloom rgba(207,230,255,.5) 3 px; fresh echo #dff3ff → after 150 ms #d8e07a (yellow-green) → #7a8a3a → #2d3418 → black over one revolution; range rings #3a5a3a at 60 %; heading marker #9ad0a0 thin line to 12 o'clock; EBL #e8ffb0 dashed; VRM ring #e8ffb0 dotted; sea clutter speckle #6b7a3a near the centre; bearing ring #f0efe8 on #111; hood #050505 → transparent vignette; console #7c8a92
- typeface: bearing numerals every 10° in a monoline engraved sans → Barlow 500, 7 px, white; the "EBL 047°" / "VRM 3.2 NM" readouts as small engraved plates below → Barlow 500, 7 px
- the tells:
  1. two-colour persistence: the sweep paints echoes in a cold blue-white flash that immediately turns yellow-green and then fades slowly — every echo is a blue tip on a yellow tail
  2. the sweep line itself is a thin bright radius with a soft bloom, and just behind it the newest returns are brightest
  3. echoes decay over one full revolution so the last-painted sector is bright and the sector ahead of the sweep is nearly gone — a wedge of brightness follows the sweep
  4. a coastline: a ragged band of echo along one side, with dark shadow behind headlands
  5. four faint range rings, a heading marker straight up, an EBL you can set to a bearing, and a VRM ring
  6. sea clutter: a fuzzy speckled disc around the centre that the sweep repaints every pass
  7. the black rubber hood ring around the screen, dark and soft-edged, so the screen seems deep in a tunnel
  8. the bearing scale engraved around the outside in white, 0 at the top
- motion: sweep at `rpm` (24 → 2.5 s per revolution), constant; echoes render on a persistent canvas with a per-frame decay (multiply by ~0.97 at 60 fps plus a colour shift from blue to yellow-green in the first 150 ms); clutter re-randomised each pass; ships (targets) creep a few px per revolution
- states to show: coast plus three targets, sweep running; EBL and VRM set on a target; short range with heavy clutter
- priority: A

### H13.2 · Furuno green raster PPI with range rings, VRM/EBL text and sea clutter
- slug: `radar-ppi-furuno-raster`
- element: `sk-radar-ppi-furuno`
- kind: output
- value: waveform count 360 (echo range per degree); attributes `targets`, `range` NM default 12, `rings` NM default 2, `ebl`, `vrm`, `gain` 0…1 (clutter amount)
- machine: Furuno FR-8000 / FR-1500 series raster-scan marine radar — a green daylight-viewable tube in a beige console with text readouts drawn on screen and soft keys along the edge
- era: 1980s
- origin: Japan
- size: ~10" screen → build at 360 × 300 px natural (round PPI Ø 260 at left, text column at right)
- materials: a rectangular green monochrome CRT with a flat anti-glare face in a beige plastic bezel; the PPI drawn as a circle with the sweep; a text column of readouts to the right; no hood
- palette: screen #061109; PPI echoes #4dff7a at 8 brightness levels (#173a24 → #4dff7a), no colour shift; sweep line #7dffa0 thin; rings and bearing marks #1f6b38; text #4dff7a; bezel #d6ccb4 with #a89c84 shadow; soft-key labels #222 on the bezel
- typeface: on-screen readouts in a dot-matrix character generator → Share Tech Mono, 9 px, uppercase ("RANGE 12 NM", "RINGS 2 NM", "VRM 3.25 NM", "EBL 047.5", "HDG 312", "GAIN"); bezel legends Inter 500 6.5 px
- the tells:
  1. raster, not persistence: echoes stay at full brightness until the next sweep overwrites them — no fading tail; the sweep line simply repaints
  2. eight discrete brightness levels of green, so echoes are quantised blocks, not soft blobs
  3. a column of text readouts in a monospaced dot font to the right of the circle, always on
  4. sea clutter near the centre as a speckled disc whose density follows `gain`
  5. a flat rectangular screen with the round PPI drawn in it and the corners unused (dark green)
  6. the bezel is beige plastic with soft keys, no hood, no engraved ring
  7. a small scan-line texture across the whole screen
- motion: sweep at 24 rpm; echoes written in the sweep's wake and held until overwritten; clutter re-randomised per pass; text updates instantly when attributes change
- states to show: 12 NM with coast and targets; 3 NM with heavy clutter; EBL/VRM on a target
- priority: B

- palette: backplate #efe9d8; scales #222; glass highlight #ffffff 50 %; mercury #b8bcc4 → #e8eaee with a bright meniscus; spirit #7a2020 (tinted) at low opacity; index pins #24304a with a lighter tip #4a5a80; bulbs glass #dfe6ea; magnet button #333 with a #777 rim; "MAX" / "MIN" legends #222
- typeface: scale numerals in a plain grotesque → Roboto Condensed 500, 6.5 px; "MAX", "MIN", "RESET" in Roboto Condensed 700, 7 px
- the tells:
  1. a U tube with mercury in the bottom and two columns that read opposite ways — the left scale runs upside down
  2. two little dark pins sitting above the mercury in each limb, left behind at the extremes
  3. the mercury is silver with a bright meniscus; the spirit above is barely visible
  4. a big bulb at the top of each limb, one full and one part-full
  5. a black round magnet button used to reset, with a small arrow
  6. the pins stay put while the mercury moves away from them
- motion: current temperature eases over ~1 s; a pin moves only when the mercury pushes it; `activate` on RESET slides both pins to the mercury over ~400 ms
- states to show: current 18 with max 27 / min 9; after a reset (pins on the mercury); a cold night (min pin far down)
- priority: B

### I1.3 · Clinical mercury thermometer with the prism stem
- slug: `thermometer-clinical-mercury`
- element: `sk-thermometer-clinical`
- kind: output

- machine: the triangular-section clinical thermometer (B-D, Zeal, Soviet Клинский) — a 4" glass rod with a prism face that magnifies the mercury thread, an arrow at normal, a chrome or Bakelite case
- era: 1950s
- origin: UK
- size: 110 × 8 mm → build at 300 × 28 px natural (horizontal); optional case below
- materials: clear glass rod with one flat face; a white opal backing strip inside; a hair-thin mercury thread magnified by the prism face into a broad silver band; etched black scale with tiny numerals; a red arrow at 37 °C; a small bulb at the left end with a constriction (the kink) just above it
- palette: glass #e9eef0 with a strong highlight #ffffff and an edge #b7c2c6; opal backing #fbfbf7; mercury magnified #c4c8cf → #eef0f3 with a dark edge #6a6f78; scale #1a1a1a; arrow #c8231d; bulb #b0b4bb
- typeface: numerals in a tiny condensed sans → Archivo Narrow 500, 5 px; every 0.5° a longer tick, every 0.1° a short one
- the tells:
  1. the magnified thread: the mercury looks like a wide silver band only when viewed through the prism face; a `tilt` attribute (0…1) narrows it to a hairline as the stem is rotated
  2. a red arrow at 37 (or 98.6) and a tightly etched scale with tiny numerals
  3. the kink — a visible narrowing just above the bulb — and the thread stops there when shaken down
  4. a long highlight the full length of the glass, and a small round bulb at the left
  5. the thread ends in a flat top, not a rounded meniscus
- motion: rises over ~30 s in real life — demo eases over 3 s; a `shake` method snaps the thread back to 35 with a small overshoot
- states to show: 36.8; 39.4 (fever); shaken down at 35 with `tilt` 0.6
- priority: C

## I2 · Sight glass / liquid level

### I2.1 · Locomotive boiler gauge glass with brass cocks and the diagonal-stripe trick
- slug: `sight-glass-boiler-gauge-brass`
- element: `sk-sight-glass-boiler`
- kind: output
- value: range min 0 max 1 step 0.005 (water level in the glass); attribute `boil` 0…1 adds bubbles and level surge
- machine: the steam-locomotive / stationary-boiler tubular water gauge (Klinger, Penberthy, GWR/LMS pattern) — a vertical glass between two brass gauge cocks with handles, a protector shield, a white backplate with diagonal black stripes
- era: 1920s
- origin: UK
- size: glass ⅝" × 10" between fittings ~ 14" tall → build at 90 × 320 px natural
- materials: a heavy brass top cock and bottom cock with turned bodies, packing nuts and long lever handles; a glass tube between them; a white enamelled backplate behind the glass printed with diagonal black stripes; a glass or wire protector shield in a brass frame in front; a drain cock at the bottom with a small pipe
- palette: brass #c9a24c → #8a6d2c → #e8cf7a highlights, with verdigris #5f8a6a in the threads; glass highlight #ffffff 50 % left, shadow #7a8a90 right; water #2a4a5a tinted at 55 % with a meniscus line #a8c8d0; backplate #f0ece0; stripes #222; the stripes appear to reverse direction where water is (refraction) — draw the stripes mirrored inside the water portion; steam above the water slightly whiter than the backplate; shield frame #b8923c
- typeface: none on the glass; an engraved brass plate "GAUGE GLASS" in a Clarendon-ish → Roboto Condensed 700, 6 px, black-filled (no slab serif on the allowed list; note it)
- the tells:
  1. the diagonal stripes on the backplate flip direction where the water is — the water column shows the stripes leaning the other way, so the level is a hard line where the stripes reverse
  2. two big brass cocks top and bottom with long handles pointing the same way (open), packing nuts, and a drain cock with a pipe at the bottom
  3. the meniscus: a slight bright curve at the water surface with a dark line under it
  4. the glass tube's highlight line the full height and the shield glass in front with its own reflection
  5. brass is polished on the handles (hands) and dull with verdigris in the threads
  6. with `boil`, the level surges ±3 % and small bubbles rise
  7. a red (or black) line on the backplate marking the lowest safe level
- motion: level eases over ~800 ms; `boil` adds a 0.6 Hz surge and bubbles at ~2/s
- states to show: half glass; low (near the danger line); boiling hard at two-thirds
- priority: A

### I4.1 · GWR lower-quadrant home signal with spectacle plate and lamp
- slug: `semaphore-gwr-lower-quadrant`

- machine: Great Western Railway lower-quadrant semaphore (Saxby & Farmer / GWR pattern) — a red arm with a white band pivoted at the post, a spectacle plate with red and blue glasses in front of an oil lamp, a white post with a black band and a finial
- era: 1900s
- origin: UK
- size: arm 4 ft × 10", post section ~ 6 ft → build at 200 × 260 px natural (arm 130 × 24 px, pivot at 60 px from the left, post 14 px wide)
- materials: a pressed-steel arm painted signal red with a white vertical band near the tip, its back white with a black band; a cast spectacle plate with two glass lenses (red and blue) rotating with the arm; a square lamp case with a lens behind the spectacle; a white-painted post with a black lower band and a cast finial on top; a balance weight lever at the foot
- palette: arm red #c8231d with wear #9a1a13 and a white band #f2f0e8; arm edge #6a1010; spectacle casting #1f1f1f; red glass #ff2a1e lit / #6a1512 unlit; blue glass #2a4aa8 lit-as-green → #34d97a (blue glass + yellow flame = green) / #1d2f5c unlit; lamp case #1f1f1f with a brass rim; post #f2f0e8 with the band #1f1f1f; finial #1f1f1f; sky #cfe0ea
- typeface: none (a small cast plate on the post → Oswald 600 5 px, white on black)
- the tells:
  1. the arm drops to show clear — 45° downward, the GWR way; horizontal is danger
  2. the spectacle plate swings with the arm so the lamp shows red through the red glass at danger and green through the blue glass at clear (the yellow flame through blue)
  3. a white band near the tip of the red arm, and the arm's back is white with a black band when seen from behind
  4. a white post with a black band at the bottom and a pointed finial on top
  5. motion: the arm falls to clear with a little bounce and springs back up to danger faster (the balance weight)
  6. the distant variant: yellow arm with a fishtail notch and a black chevron, yellow and green glasses
  7. at night the arm is a silhouette and only the lamp aspect shows
- motion: on → off: arm rotates 45° down over ~600 ms with a 4° overshoot and settle; off → on: up over ~350 ms with a hard stop and a 1 px shudder; the spectacle rotates with it; `night` crossfades the lamp
- states to show: on (danger); off (clear); night off (green lamp); distant on
- priority: A

## I5 · Reel / spool

### I5.1 · Ampex 10½" NAB reel on the three-lobed hub knob
- slug: `reel-ampex-nab-10in`
- element: `sk-reel-ampex-nab`
- kind: output
- value: range min 0 max 1 step 0.001 (tape on this reel — sets the pack radius); attribute `rate` rev/s (signed, default 0), `playing` boolean; attribute `role` = supply | takeup for the pack direction
- machine: Ampex 350 / AG-440 / ATR-100 with Ampex precision 10½" aluminium reels on NAB hub adapters — the three-lobed spring hub knob and the amber tape pack showing through the three big windows
- era: 1970s
- origin: USA
- size: reel Ø 267 mm → build at 240 × 240 px natural
- materials: a machined aluminium reel with three wide spokes and three large windows, a brushed rim; a black NAB hub adapter with a three-lobed knurled knob and a centre screw; the tape pack (brown oxide edge) seen through the windows and its outer edge visible past the hub; a grey-green deck plate behind
- palette: reel #d9dadb → #9c9fa2 with a circular brushed anisotropy (a bright arc that stays fixed while the reel turns); window edges #6c7073; tape pack #6b3f1a → #a0682d with a fine concentric ring texture and a bright edge ring #c9925a; hub #1e1e20 with knurl highlights #4a4a4e; screw #cfcfd0; deck #7f8c86
- typeface: the reel's engraved wordmark generic in Josefin Sans 600 6 px, dark, on one spoke
- the tells:
  1. three wide spokes and three big windows — the pack shows as an amber-brown ring through the windows and grows/shrinks with `value`
  2. the three-lobed hub knob in the middle, black with knurled lobes and a centre screw, turning with the reel
  3. the reel turns but its brushed-metal highlight arc stays put (it is a reflection, not a mark)
  4. the tape pack has a fine ring grain and a darker inner edge near the hub
  5. rotation rate depends on pack radius: a supply reel speeds up as it empties (rate ∝ 1/radius at constant tape speed)
  6. at fast wind the spokes blur into a grey ring; at play they are crisp
  7. a hard shadow under the reel on the deck plate
- motion: rotation at `rate`; when `playing`, `value` drifts (supply down, take-up up) and `rate` follows 1/radius; motion blur above ~2 rev/s via a low-opacity double image; spin-down over ~1.5 s on stop
- states to show: full pack still; playing at 15 ips; fast forward (blurred); nearly empty
- priority: A

### I5.2 · IBM 729 tape drive with vacuum columns
- slug: `reel-ibm-729-vacuum-columns`
- element: `sk-reel-ibm-729`
- kind: output
- value: range min 0 max 1 step 0.001 (tape position, share on the right reel); attribute `activity` = idle | read | rewind
- machine: IBM 729 / 2401 half-inch tape drive — two 10½" reels behind a glass door with two vacuum columns below in which loops of tape hang and jerk; the stop-start motion of every 1960s movie computer
- era: 1960s
- origin: USA
- size: the upper cabinet ~ 600 × 900 mm → build at 240 × 360 px natural (two reels Ø 96 at the top, two columns 28 × 180 below)
- materials: a blue-grey steel cabinet with a glass door; two plastic reels (one with a coloured hub band); the tape running down through a head block into two glass-fronted vacuum columns with slotted metal walls; a lit status strip
- palette: cabinet #4f6f8a (IBM blue-grey) with a #3a5268 shadow; glass reflection #ffffff 10 % diagonal; reels #d9d9d6 with hub bands #c8231d (file protect ring) / #1f1f1f; tape #3a2a1e; columns interior #1a1a1c with slots #2c2c30; column glass highlight; lamps #ffd27a
- typeface: a small "SELECT" / "READY" legend strip → Inter 500, 6 px, white on black
- the tells:
  1. two loops of tape hanging in the vacuum columns that rise and fall independently — the loops jerk up when a reel feeds and sag as the capstan takes
  2. the reels start and stop in bursts — a burst of spin, then still, then a burst
  3. the tape runs from the top reel down into one column, up over the head, down the other column, up to the other reel
  4. glass door with a diagonal reflection; blue-grey cabinet
  5. a red file-protect ring on one reel hub
  6. rewind: both reels blur and the loops flatten to the top of the columns
- motion: `read`: random bursts of 200–800 ms of reel motion with the loops moving out of phase; `rewind`: continuous fast spin with blur; `idle`: loops drift slowly
- states to show: idle; reading (bursts); rewinding
- priority: B

- the tells:

  2. the tape visible as a dark band running across the bottom past the pressure pad
  3. a clear shell: you see the inside, the rollers, the five screws at the corners and centre
  4. the smoked window darkens and desaturates it all and adds a soft top reflection
  5. at fast wind the hub teeth blur and the packs visibly move over a few seconds
- motion: hubs rotate at rates ∝ 1/pack radius; `rate` scales; motion blur on the teeth above 3 rev/s
- states to show: at the start (left full); mid-tape playing; fast-forward
- priority: B

## I6 · Pendulum / metronome / balance wheel

### I6.1 · Wittner Maelzel pyramid metronome, walnut, with the sliding weight
- slug: `metronome-wittner-maelzel`
- element: `sk-metronome-wittner`
- kind: both
- value: range min 40 max 208 step 1 unit bpm (the weight's position; drag the weight or use the keyboard); attribute `running` boolean; attribute `bell` = 0 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 6 (accent every n beats)
- machine: Wittner "Maelzel" 803 / 811 pyramid metronome (also Seth Thomas) — the wooden pyramid case with the front door off, showing an inverted pendulum with a brass sliding weight against a printed tempo scale, a wind-up key on the side
- era: 1950s
- origin: Germany
- size: case 220 mm tall × 120 wide at the base → build at 140 × 240 px natural (pendulum 180 px long from its pivot near the base)
- materials: a walnut-veneered pyramid case with a satin finish, the front opening framed by a lip; a printed cream scale card with tempo numbers and names; a steel pendulum rod with a brass sliding weight (a trapezoid with a window) and a black lead bob at the bottom behind the base; a brass key on the right side; a small bell lever
- palette: walnut #4a2c1a → #7a4a2c with grain; the lip #2e1a10; scale card #efe6c8 with print #222; rod #9a9a9a with a highlight; weight brass #c9a24c → #8a6d2c with a window; bob #1a1a1a; key #c9a24c
- typeface: tempo numerals in a condensed sans → Archivo Narrow 600, 6.5 px (40 42 44 46 48 50 52 54 56 58 60 63 66 69 72 76 80 84 88 92 96 100 104 108 112 116 120 126 132 138 144 152 160 168 176 184 192 200 208); tempo names ("Largo", "Larghetto", "Adagio", "Andante", "Moderato", "Allegro", "Presto", "Prestissimo") in Archivo Narrow 400 italic, 6 px, beside the scale
- the tells:
  1. the pendulum is upside down — the rod swings from a pivot near the base and the weight slides on the upper part against the scale; higher = slower
  2. the brass weight has a little window showing the tempo number it sits on
  3. the tick is visible: at each extreme the rod stops dead for a frame (the escapement) before swinging back
  4. the swing amplitude is wide (~±35°) and constant; only the period changes with the weight
  5. a walnut pyramid with the door off, the scale card inside slightly yellowed
  6. the brass wind-up key on the side and the bell lever with its numbers
  7. the numerals are not evenly spaced — larger steps at the top
- motion: while `running`, the rod swings with a half-period of 60/bpm s using a near-sinusoid with a hard stop at each extreme (a 30 ms hold); dragging the weight (vertical) changes bpm live; a `bell` accent flashes the bell lever
- states to show: stopped at 60; running at 120; running at 208 (weight at the bottom)
- priority: A

## I7 · Spinning disc / turntable / platter

### I7.1 · Technics SL-1200 MK2 platter rim with four strobe rows and the neon lamp
- slug: `platter-technics-sl1200-strobe`
- element: `sk-platter-sl1200-strobe`
- kind: output
- value: range min −8 max 8 step 0.05 unit % (pitch); attributes `rpm` = 33 | 45, `mains` = 50 | 60, `running` boolean
- machine: Technics SL-1200 MK2 / SL-1210 — the diecast platter with four rows of strobe dots cast into its rim, lit by the red-orange neon in the black housing at front-left; the dots freeze at the correct speed and drift with pitch
- era: 1970s
- origin: Japan
- size: the front-left quadrant of a Ø 332 mm platter with the strobe housing → build at 320 × 140 px natural (a 90° arc of rim, 36 px deep, with the housing 40 × 28 at the left)
- materials: a diecast aluminium platter with a satin finish and a raised rim carrying four rows of dots (cast, then painted black between); the rubber mat's edge just visible above; a black plastic strobe housing with a rectangular window and the neon inside; the silver diecast plinth with a fine matte texture; a "33 / 45" legend beside the rows
- palette: platter rim #c9cbcd → #8f9295 satin with a fixed highlight arc; dots #f2f2f0 on the black bands #1a1a1c; mat edge #1e1e1e; housing #141416 with a #2c2c30 edge; neon window #ff6a2a → #ff9a5c with a faint 100/120 Hz flicker and a warm spill onto the rim rgba(255,120,60,.35); plinth #d4d5d3 with a grain
- typeface: "33 / 45" and the row legends in a rounded Eurostile-like → Michroma 400, 5.5 px, white; the wordmark generic
- the tells:
  1. four rows of dots on the rim, each with a different pitch (for 33 and 45 at 50 and 60 Hz); at the right speed one row stands still while the others crawl
  2. the neon is red-orange and flickers at mains rate — it is what makes the dots strobe; render the dots as a texture whose apparent drift = (actual dot rate − mains strobe rate)
  3. pitch off zero: the frozen row drifts forward (+) or backward (−), faster with more pitch
  4. the rim highlight is fixed while the dots move under it
  5. a black rubber mat edge above the rim with a fine radial rib pattern
  6. the housing's window glows and spills orange onto the platter rim
  7. spin-up: on `running` the dots accelerate over ~0.7 s (the 1200's direct drive is quick) and settle
- motion: dot texture translates along the arc at (row rate · (1 + pitch/100) − strobe rate) px/s; the correct row for `rpm`/`mains` is frozen at pitch 0; the neon flickers 2 % at 100/120 Hz; spin-up 0.7 s, spin-down ~2 s
- states to show: 33 at 0 % (one row frozen); +3 % (drift); stopped; 45 at 60 Hz
- priority: A

- era: 1940s
- origin: USA
- size: the door window ~ 180 × 220 mm in a 220 × 300 case → build at 240 × 320 px natural (paper 180 × 240 visible)
- materials: a black wrinkle-painted steel case with a chrome-plated door frame and a glass door (with a reflection); cream chart paper with a green printed grid whose "vertical" lines are arcs (the pen pivots, so the grid is curvilinear) and horizontal time lines; a black pen arm pivoting from the right edge with a small glass ink capillary and a red ink trace; a brass ink well; the paper drum at the top and the take-up spool below
- palette: case #1c1c1c with a wrinkle web #2e2e2e and highlights #4a4a4a on the ridges; door frame chrome #e8e8e8 / #7a7a7a; glass reflection #ffffff 10 % diagonal; paper #efe6cc; grid #5aa06a at 55 % (fine) and #3d8a4e (every 10th); time lines the same, horizontal; trace #c8181a 1.2 px with a slightly darker #9a1214 edge where the pen paused; pen arm #1a1a1a; capillary glass #cfe0e8; ink well brass #c9a24c
- typeface: the grid's printed scale 0…100 along the top edge in a small grotesque → Libre Franklin 500, 5.5 px, green; the maker's chart legend "CHART No. 123" in Special Elite 6 px
- the tells:
  1. the grid is curvilinear: the value lines are arcs centred on the pen pivot, so a constant value is an arc and the pen's path is an arc — a straight vertical line on this paper is wrong
  2. the paper moves downward (time runs down), the pen writes at a fixed height near the top of the window
  3. the trace is red ink: it is thicker where the pen moved slowly and has a small blob where it paused, thinner on fast excursions
  4. a black wrinkle case with a chrome door frame and glass in front with a diagonal reflection
  5. the pen arm pivots from the side, a long thin black arm with a glass capillary at its tip
  6. green grid on cream paper, the heavy line every 10 divisions and a time stamp every hour
  7. the paper's edge shows perforations (sprocket drive) at one side
- motion: paper scrolls at `speed`; the pen arm rotates about its pivot to the current value (the tip follows an arc) with a 150 ms lag and a slight overshoot; the trace is drawn onto a persistent canvas that scrolls with the paper
- states to show: a slow varying signal; a step response with a pen overshoot blob; a long steady line with the paper perforations

### I9.2 · Twin-gong trembler electric bell with the exposed coils
- slug: `bell-trembler-twin-gong`
- element: `sk-bell-trembler`
- kind: output
- value: boolean (ringing)
- machine: the classic school / doorbell trembler bell (Edwards, GPO, the physics-lesson bell) — two brass gongs on a wooden or Bakelite base with a hammer vibrating between them, the electromagnet coils and contact screw exposed
- era: 1920s
- origin: UK
- size: base ~ 120 × 80 mm → build at 200 × 140 px natural (two gongs Ø 56 at the top corners, the coils and armature between)
- materials: a varnished wooden base (or brown Bakelite) with two brass terminals; two spun brass gongs on posts; a black steel armature on a spring with a small round hammer head between the gongs; two electromagnet coils wrapped in black waxed paper with the iron cores visible; a contact screw with a lock nut
- palette: wood #8a5a2c with grain and varnish gloss; brass #c9a24c → #8a6d2c with #fff2c0 highlights, one gong a little duller (different age); coils #1f1a16 with a paper texture and a #3a332c highlight; cores #6e6e6e; armature #2a2a2e; contact screw #cfcfd0; terminals #c9a24c
- typeface: none (a small paper label "6 V" in Special Elite 5 px)
- the tells:
  1. two gongs, and the hammer shuttles between them so fast it is a blur — the sound is the two-note trembler
  2. the mechanism is naked: two black coils, an iron armature, a spring, a contact screw with a tiny spark
  3. brass gongs with a spun finish (fine concentric lines) and a slot on top where the post holds them
  4. a wooden base with two brass terminals and a bit of bare wire
  5. ringing, both gongs shake and the armature blurs; a small spark flickers at the contact
- motion: `ringing`: the armature alternates position every frame (~30 Hz), each gong shakes 1–2 px, a spark flickers randomly at the contact; stop is instant with a 200 ms gong ring-down
- states to show: silent; ringing
- priority: B

### I9.3 · Twin-bell alarm clock with the hammer (Westclox / Слава)
- slug: `bell-alarm-clock-twin`
- element: `sk-bell-alarm-clock-twin`
- kind: output
- value: boolean (ringing); attribute `time` "HH:MM" for the face (drawn as a simple clock, F12 crossover kept minimal)
- machine: the twin-bell mechanical alarm clock — Westclox "Bradley", the German "Peter", the Soviet Слава — two chrome or brass bells on top with a hammer between, a round case on two feet
- era: 1960s
- origin: USSR
- size: case Ø 110 mm plus bells → build at 140 × 160 px natural
- materials: a round pressed-steel case in cream or red enamel with a chrome bezel and a domed glass; two chrome-plated bells on posts on top with a black hammer between; two small chrome feet; a plain white dial with black numerals and a red alarm hand
- palette: case #e8e0c8 (cream) or #c8231d (Soviet red); bezel and bells chrome #f4f4f4 → #9a9a9a → #3a3a3a; hammer #1a1a1a; dial #f6f4ec with numerals #1a1a1a; hands #1a1a1a, alarm hand #c8231d; glass highlight #ffffff 30 % arc
- typeface: dial numerals in a plain grotesque → Roboto Condensed 500, 8 px; a generic wordmark on the dial in Noto Sans 500, 5 px (Cyrillic variant "СЛАВА"-style replaced by generic)
- the tells:
  1. two bells on top with a hammer between; ringing, the hammer is a blur and the whole clock hops
  2. chrome bells with a bright dome highlight and a dark reflected band, each on a short post
  3. a domed glass over a plain dial, with a big arc highlight
  4. two little chrome feet, and the clock rocks on them when ringing
  5. the red alarm hand on the dial

## I10 · Sandglass / egg timer

### I10.1 · Naval half-hour glass in a turned-wood pillar frame
- slug: `sandglass-naval-pillar-frame`
- element: `sk-sandglass-naval`
- kind: both
- value: time (seconds remaining in the top bulb, counting down while `running`); attribute `duration` s default 1800 (demo shorter); click or Space flips the glass (emits `activate` and restarts)
- machine: the ship's watch glass of the 17th–19th centuries — two blown-glass bulbs bound at the waist with cord, in a turned-wood frame of four pillars with round end plates, white sand
- era: pre-1900
- origin: UK
- size: ~ 200 mm tall × 90 wide → build at 100 × 220 px natural
- materials: two hand-blown glass bulbs (slightly asymmetric, with a seed bubble or two) joined at a narrow waist wrapped in waxed cord; fine white-grey sand; a frame of four turned pillars (beads and rings) in dark oak between two round end plates with a hole through the middle; brass pins at the plate edges
- palette: glass highlight #ffffff 45 % long streaks and a #b8c4c8 edge; sand #e8e2d0 with grain noise and a #cfc8b4 shadow side; the falling stream #e8e2d0 1 px; cord #5a4a30; wood #3a2a1a → #6b4a2c with turned highlights; brass pins #c9a24c
- typeface: none (a small engraved brass plate "½ HOUR" in Special Elite 5 px optional)
- the tells:
  1. two bulbs and a waist bound with cord — the cord and the slightly uneven hand-blown glass are what say "old"
  2. the sand in the top bulb sinks as a cone with a dimple in the middle; the sand in the bottom builds as a cone with a peak; a thin stream between
  3. four turned pillars with beads, and round end plates — the frame is dark turned wood
  4. flipping: the whole glass rotates 180° in the frame (the frame rotates with it), the sand cones swap, and the stream restarts after a beat
  5. the last grains: the top cone narrows to a small pile that suddenly empties
  6. long vertical highlights on both bulbs; a seed bubble in the glass
- motion: sand transfers at a constant rate over `duration`; the top cone's dimple deepens and the bottom peak rises; the stream stops when the top is empty; flip = 180° rotation over ~500 ms with an ease, then the stream begins after 200 ms
- states to show: just flipped (full top); half; last grains; empty
- priority: A

- element: `sk-sandglass-boggle`

- palette: plastic #ffffff 20 % with a #cfd8dc edge and seam lines #b0bcc2; sand #f4f0e8 (white) or #f2a4c0 (pink); stream 1 px; the end discs #e8ecee 40 %

## I11 · Mechanical wave / bar indicator

### I11.1 · Marvy chrome barber pole with the lit globe and climbing helix
- slug: `barber-pole-marvy-chrome`
- element: `sk-barber-pole-marvy`
- kind: output
- value: boolean (running: motor and light); attribute `rate` stripes/s default 1, `stripes` = rwb | rw
- machine: William Marvy Co. (St Paul) Model 55 / 405 barber pole — a glass cylinder with a red-white-blue helix rotating inside, a chrome-plated cast housing top and bottom, a lit glass globe on top
- era: 1950s
- origin: USA
- size: cylinder Ø 150 × 500 mm, with cap and globe ~ 750 mm → build at 120 × 300 px natural (globe Ø 60 at the top, cylinder 80 × 180, base 120 × 40)
- materials: a clear glass cylinder with a slight green tint at the edges; inside, a printed helical sleeve (red, white, blue diagonal stripes at ~30°) on a motor; a chrome-plated cast-aluminium cap and base with fluted decoration and a mounting bracket; a frosted white glass globe on top lit from inside
- palette: glass highlights #ffffff 45 % two vertical streaks and a #a8b8b0 edge; stripes red #c8231d, white #f6f4ee, blue #1f3b8a, with a cylindrical shading (darker at the edges, a highlight band left of centre) applied over the stripes; chrome #f4f4f4 → #9a9a9a → #3a3a3a with flutes; globe unlit #d8d8d4, lit #fff6d6 with a warm halo rgba(255,240,200,.4) 16 px; a light inside the cylinder makes the stripes glow slightly when running
- typeface: none (a small cast maker's plate on the base, generic in Josefin Sans 600 5 px)

  2. cylindrical shading over the stripes: the colours are darker at the edges and there is a fixed vertical highlight on the glass that the stripes move under
  3. a lit frosted globe on top with a warm glow, and chrome castings with flutes top and bottom

  6. the mounting bracket at the back with two bolts
- motion: stripe pattern translates upward at `rate` cycles/s (a rotating helix maps to a vertical translation of the stripe texture); the motor spins up over ~1.5 s and coasts down over ~2 s; the globe fades 200 ms

# J · Panels, furniture and housings

*Phase 3 of `../PLAN.md`, built on `p2-HIJ.md` §J1–J11 (H and I are in `p3-HIJ.md`). One entry per style, exactly one priority-A per code. Conventions for this section: the element is a swatch or a piece of furniture that other pages mount things on — `kind: output`; `value: text` is the legend printed, engraved, embossed or stamped on it (may be empty), or `boolean` where the piece has a state (lit, locked, open). Every swatch takes `width` and `height` in natural px (defaults given under size) and a `finish` attribute where the source comes in variants; a swatch must tile or stretch cleanly to any size at `scale="1"` — grain, texture and edge wear are generated (SVG filters, repeating gradients, seeded noise), never a raster. Wear, chips and peeling corners are opt-in attributes (`wear="0..1"`) so a pristine panel is also available. Machine names are for reference; builds use generic wordmarks and never a trademark logo.*

---

## J1 · Brushed / anodised aluminium

### J1.1 · Marantz champagne silver face with dark-blue Helvetica
- slug: `panel-alu-marantz-champagne`
- element: `sk-panel-alu-champagne`
- kind: output
- value: text (a silk-screened legend row, e.g. "BASS   TREBLE   BALANCE"; empty allowed); attribute `finish` = champagne | silver (Pioneer-neutral) ; attribute `lines` draws the engraved-and-filled hairline rules
- machine: Marantz 2270 / 2230 / 2325 receiver front, and the wider 1970s Japanese "silver face" (Pioneer SX-1250, Sansui 9090DB, Kenwood KA-9100)
- era: 1970s
- origin: Japan
- size: a 4 mm clear-anodised plate → build at 320 × 120 px natural (any `width` × `height`), legend baseline 14 px from the bottom edge
- materials: brushed aluminium, clear-anodised with a warm champagne-gold tint, fine horizontal grain (~0.3 mm pitch); black or dark-blue thin-film silk-screen legends; two engraved hairlines filled black running the full width; a 1 mm bright bevel on the visible edge
- palette: plate mid #d9cfb4, grain highlights #f3ecd8, grain shadows #b9ad8f, reflected band #fbf6ea at 35 % across the upper third, bevel #f7f2e4 → #8e8468; legend #1c2a4a (dark blue) or #14161a (black); hairline #23262b with a 1 px #ede6d2 light line beneath
- typeface: Helvetica-family silk-screen → Google "Inter" 500 (Libre Franklin as fallback), 9 px, tracking 0.16em, all caps; model-name badge in "Michroma" 10 px
- the tells:
  1. the grain is horizontal, continuous across the whole width, and dead straight — hundreds of hairlines of alternating light and dark, not noise; the eye reads it as a directional sheen
  2. a single soft reflected highlight band runs across the upper third and follows the grain (a horizontal blur, not a vertical one), brighter at the left
  3. the anodise is warm — a champagne gold, not neutral silver; `finish="silver"` cools it to #d4d4d0
  4. the legends are tiny, spaced wide and printed in dark blue, sitting very slightly proud of the grain (a 0.5 px darker halo under each glyph)
  5. two engraved hairlines, filled black, with a bright lower edge — they look cut in, not printed
  6. the plate edge shows a 1 px bright chamfer and the raw aluminium (whiter than the face) below it
  7. with `wear`, the legend nearest the centre knob is thinned — the ink wears through to bare grain under the thumb
- motion: none; the highlight band shifts ±6 px with `tilt` (pointer x) so the sheen moves like a real brushed surface
- states to show: 320 × 120 champagne with "BASS TREBLE BALANCE" and hairlines; a 200 × 60 silver blank; a worn one (`wear=".6"`)
- priority: A

### J1.2 · Braun fine-brushed clear anodised with tiny Akzidenz legends
- slug: `panel-alu-braun-fine-brush`
- element: `sk-panel-alu-braun`
- kind: output

  3. the colour is neutral cool grey-silver, no gold, no blue

  5. the sheen is low: a faint, wide highlight, never a hard reflected band
  6. the pale plastic cap next to the plate shows the Rams pairing — warm-white plastic against cool aluminium
  7. edges are square and crisp with a 1 px bright edge; no chamfer, no chips

- the tells:

  2. white rules box the sections with a rounded-corner rectangle and the section name sits in a gap in the top rule
  3. the legends are warm white and a Futura-like geometric with a round O and a pointed A
  4. the walnut cheek is a solid block: oiled, matt, with straight long grain and a softly rounded top corner; the plate ends in a hard black edge against it
  5. a 1 px raw-aluminium highlight where the plate edge is chamfered (bare metal shows silver through the black)
