- value: text (the stencilled legend, e.g. "NO STEP" or "USA 20-5-8"); attribute `ground` = olive | grey | green (British) | wood; attribute `paint` = white | yellow
- machine: US Army crates, jerry cans and PRC radios; USAAF "NO STEP"; British and Soviet crates — paint sprayed through a cut stencil
- era: 1940s
- origin: USA
- size: build at 20 px cap height natural (any `size`), width from the text; the ground swatch extends 16 px around
- materials: flat olive-drab enamel on steel (or raw wood); white or yellow paint sprayed through a cut card stencil: bridged letters, a soft overspray fringe, a few drips and a thin spot where the can ran out
- palette: olive #5b6b3a with a flat #52613a low and #68784a high; grey ground #6f7476; British green #3d5a3b; wood #b89a6a with grain #9c7f52; white paint #ece9de with overspray rgba(236,233,222,.35) 2 px; yellow paint #e8c23a; drips the paint colour with a darker #c9c5b8 edge
- typeface: a bridged stencil Gothic → Google "Big Shoulders" 700 (or "Anton"), 20 px, tracking 0.2em, with the bridges cut as SVG masks: a 1.5 px gap across each counter's stroke (O, A, B, D, P, R, Q, 0, 4, 6, 8, 9)
- the tells:
  1. bridges: every closed counter has a gap where the stencil card connected — the mark of a stencil, not a font
  2. the edges are soft: a 1–2 px overspray fringe outside every stroke, denser at the bottom of the letters
  3. one or two drips from the lower edge of a stroke, tapering, with a rounded end
  4. the paint is uneven — thinner (the ground showing through) in a patch where the can ran out
  5. letters are spaced wide and mechanically even; the whole line is slightly tilted
  6. the olive ground is flat matt with a faint brush texture; no sheen at all
- motion: none
- states to show: "NO STEP" white on olive; "USA 20-5-8" yellow on olive with a drip; "ВЕРХ" on wood
- priority: B

### J10.4 · Hot-stamped gold Cyrillic on black
- slug: `label-hot-stamp-gold-black`
- element: `sk-label-hot-stamp`
- kind: output
- value: text (the stamped legend, e.g. "ОКЕАН" or "ГРОМКОСТЬ"); attribute `foil` = gold | silver | cream (the Hammond brown-plate variant with `ground="brown"`)
- machine: VEF / Океан Soviet radios (gold on black), Japanese 1970s calculators (silver), Hammond plates (cream on brown) — foil pressed into plastic with heat
- era: 1970s
- origin: USSR
- size: build at 24 px tall natural, width from the text plus 16 px; the ground swatch fills the element
- materials: a metallic foil pressed into the plastic so the letters are very slightly recessed (0.1 mm) with soft edges; the foil bright and directional (it flashes at one angle); it wears off the raised parts of any texture first, leaving a ghost
- palette: black ground #1a1a1b with a #2c2c2e sheen; brown ground #3a2416; gold foil #d9b352 with a flash #f6e2a0 and a dull #a3822e; silver foil #cfd0cc / #f0f0ee / #8e8f8b; cream #ece0c2; recess shadow rgba(0,0,0,.5) 0.5 px on the upper edge; worn ghost rgba(217,179,82,.25)
- typeface: the wide Soviet grotesk → Google "Roboto Condensed" 700, 10 px, tracking 0.08em; the silver Japanese variant in "Michroma" 8 px
- the tells:
  1. the letters are metallic and directional: a diagonal flash gradient across the glyphs that shifts with `tilt`, unlike the flat printed white of a silk-screen
  2. very slightly recessed: a hairline shadow on the upper edge of each stroke and a hairline light on the lower
  3. soft edges — the foil bleeds a fraction, so the glyphs look a touch bolder than the font
  4. worn: with `wear`, parts of the foil are missing, leaving a matte ghost of the letter in the plastic (the recess remains)
  5. the ground is glossy black plastic with one soft sheen band
- motion: the foil flash follows `tilt`
- states to show: "ОКЕАН" gold on black; a worn one with missing foil; "VIBRATO" cream on brown
- priority: C

## J11 · Fasteners and furniture

### J11.1 · Screw-head set by era and country
- slug: `fastener-screw-head-set`
- element: `sk-fastener-screw`
- kind: output
- value: text (unused; empty); attribute `drive` = slotted | phillips | pozi | jis | hex | torx | thumb; attribute `head` = pan | round | oval | cheese | button; attribute `finish` = nickel | brass | black-oxide | zinc | cad-yellow | stainless; attribute `washer` = none | flat | cup | star | dress; attribute `angle` sets the slot angle
- machine: the drive recesses of a century — slotted brass on radio cabinets and Leica cheese-heads, Phillips nickel pan-heads on Tektronix and Fender, Pozidriv on Dual and Revox, JIS with its dot on Sony and Technics, black hex socket on Moog and Eurorack, Torx on 1980s automotive, cad-plated yellow on military
- era: 1950s
- origin: USA
- size: build at 16 × 16 px natural per head (Ø 12 px head); the demo lays out a 7 × 5 grid of drive × finish
- materials: a domed or flat head with a cut or pressed recess; the finish's own reflection — nickel bright with a horizon, brass warm, black oxide dull with a soft grey highlight, zinc bluish-silver, cadmium an iridescent yellow-green, stainless a cool satin; washers under the head as separate rings; a burr where a driver slipped
- palette: nickel #f0f0f0 → #9c9c9c → #3c3c3c; brass #e6c46a → #b08a3c → #6b5220; black oxide #2a2a2c with highlight #55555a; zinc #d7dde3 → #98a0a8; cad-yellow #d6c04a with #9fbf5a and #c88f3a iridescence; stainless #d2d4d4 → #9a9c9c; recess shadow #111 with a 1 px bright far wall; cup washer black nylon #1f1f21 or nickel; star washer #b9b9b9 with 12 teeth
- typeface: none
- the tells:
  1. the recess is the identity: slotted (one straight cut with bright far wall), Phillips (a cross with tapered arms and a rounded centre), Pozi (the cross plus four small 45° ticks), JIS (a Phillips-like cross with a tiny dot beside it), hex (a dark hexagonal well), Torx (a six-lobed star), thumb (a knurled ring, no recess)
  2. the head is a small dome: a highlight on the upper-left, a shadow rim lower-right, and a drop shadow onto the panel
  3. the finish is read by colour and hardness of the highlight: nickel hard and cool, brass soft and warm, black oxide nearly flat, cad-yellow with a green-to-orange shimmer
  4. slots and crosses are at random angles unless `angle` is set — a row of aligned slots is the tell of a museum restoration, not of use
  5. a washer under the head is a separate ring: the cup washer (a black nylon dish for rack screws), the flat, the star (12 sharp teeth), the dress washer (a wide bright chrome ring)
  6. with `wear`, a burr — a small bright scar on the head where a driver slipped — and a ring of rust or grime around a slotted brass one
- motion: none
- states to show: the 7 × 5 grid; a 10-32 black rack screw with a cup washer at 24 px; a brass slotted with a cup washer; a cad-yellow Phillips with a star washer
- priority: A

### J11.2 · Dzus quarter-turn row on a dimpled aircraft panel
- slug: `fastener-dzus-quarter-turn-row`
- element: `sk-fastener-dzus-row`
- kind: output
- value: boolean (locked — all buttons turned to the locked mark; per-button state via `open="1,3"`); attribute `count` sets the number of buttons
- machine: Dzus quarter-turn fasteners (1932) on aircraft access panels and race-car body panels; Camloc flush fasteners on jets (`style="camloc"`)
- era: 1940s
- origin: USA
- size: each button Ø 10 mm in a dimple → build at 24 × 24 px per button on a 40 px pitch; the demo strip 6 buttons wide on a 260 × 40 px painted panel with a lap edge
- materials: a round flush stainless button with a curved (partial-spiral) slot and a small arrow or dot at its rim marking the locked position; the skin dimpled around it (a soft ring shadow); a row of them along a panel edge with the panel's lap joint and a paint line; Camloc: a cross-slot flush head
- palette: button stainless #d9dbdb → #a5a8a8 → #4a4d4d; slot #151617 with a bright far wall #e9ebeb 1 px; dimple ring shadow rgba(0,0,0,.28) 3 px with a highlight #ffffff at 20 % on the far side; panel olive #5b6b3a or grey #8a8f92 or natural alclad #c9cccd; lap-joint shadow #2f3335 1 px; locked mark #e8e8e8 dot
- typeface: none; an optional stencilled "NO STEP" (J10.3) beside the row
- the tells:
  1. the slot is curved — a partial spiral, not a straight line — and turns 90° between open and locked
  2. each button sits in a soft dimple: a ring of shadow on the near side and a faint highlight on the far side
  3. a tiny dot or arrow on the button's rim lines up with a mark on the panel when locked
  4. the row is straight and evenly spaced along a panel edge, with the lap joint visible as a hairline shadow
  5. the buttons are stainless-bright against a matt painted or dull alclad skin; one has a scratched ring where a driver slipped
  6. open buttons stand a fraction proud (a 1 px stronger shadow) and their slots are turned 90°
- motion: on `value` change each button turns 90° over ~180 ms, staggered 40 ms along the row
- states to show: 6 locked on olive; the same with 2 and 4 open; the Camloc variant on grey
- priority: B

### J11.3 · 1U black rack blank with ears and cup-washer screws
- slug: `furniture-rack-blank-1u`
- element: `sk-furniture-rack-blank`
- kind: output
- value: text (a Dymo or engraved strip legend, e.g. "SPARE"; empty allowed); attribute `units` = 1 | 2 | 3; attribute `finish` = black-anodised | grey-enamel (1960s telco) | vented (a row of slots); attribute `rails` draws the rack rails behind
- machine: the 19" EIA rack blank panel and its ears — 1.75" per unit, four slotted holes, 10-32 screws with black cup washers; the 1980s black rack
- era: 1980s
- origin: USA
- size: 19" × 1.75" → build at 482 × 44 px natural per unit; ears 16 px wide each side; holes 8 × 6 px slots inset 6 px
- materials: a black-anodised brushed aluminium panel (fine horizontal grain) with a folded steel ear at each end; four slotted rack holes with black 10-32 screws in black nylon cup washers; rack rails behind with tapped holes (or square cage-nut holes) showing through the slots; a Dymo strip or an engraved lamacoid ID
- palette: black anodise #1c1d1f with grain #2a2b2e / #121314 and a #3a3b3f sheen band; grey enamel #8a8f92 with #a0a5a8 high; ear edge #3a3a3c with a 1 px bare-aluminium highlight #b0b0b0; slot interior #08090a; rail behind #2e2f31 with holes #0a0a0b; screw black #202022 with a #4a4a4e highlight; cup washer #1a1a1c with a #333336 rim
- typeface: the strip's Dymo (J10.2) or engraved Barlow (J10.1)
- the tells:
  1. the proportions: a long thin panel, 11 : 1 for 1U, with the ears flush to the face and the holes in vertical slots so the panel can slide
  2. four black screws in black nylon cup washers — the washer a shallow dish, wider than the head, with a soft rim highlight
  3. the slot shows the rack rail behind through the gap not covered by the washer
  4. the grain runs horizontally along the panel, and the ears (folded steel, painted) have no grain
  5. a hairline of bare aluminium along the folded edge and the punched slot edges
  6. a slightly crooked Dymo strip or a screwed lamacoid ID near the left ear
  7. the vented variant has a row of horizontal slots with dark interiors; the grey-enamel variant swaps the grain for a satin enamel with chips at the ears
- motion: none
- states to show: 1U black with "SPARE" on Dymo; 2U vented; 1U grey enamel with a lamacoid ID
- priority: B

### J11.4 · Grille swatches — punched steel, silver-sparkle cloth, basketweave
- slug: `furniture-grille-swatch-trio`
- element: `sk-furniture-grille`
- kind: output
- value: text (unused; empty); attribute `pattern` = punched (Braun round holes in a square grid) | sparkle (Fender silver-and-black weave) | basketweave (Marshall) | honeycomb (1970s Japanese hex) | expanded (diamond expanded metal) | louvre (stamped steel louvres)
- machine: Braun SK 4 / TS 45 punched-steel grilles; Fender 1964– silver-sparkle grille cloth; Marshall basketweave (1969–); Pioneer honeycomb; Peavey expanded metal; 1960s TV louvred vents
- era: 1960s
- origin: Germany
- size: build at 160 × 160 px natural (tiles to any size); punched holes Ø 6 px on an 8 px grid; sparkle weave 4 px pitch; basketweave 12 px blocks; hex 10 px; expanded 12 × 6 px diamonds; louvres 6 px pitch
- materials: punched: a pale-grey painted steel sheet with round holes showing a dark interior and a bright lower rim on each hole; sparkle: a woven cloth of silver metallic and black threads with a faint blue-grey cast, the weave sparkling at the crossings; basketweave: a coarse woven cloth in black and dark-brown with a checked structure; honeycomb: black hex mesh; expanded: cut-and-stretched steel with a twist to each strand; louvre: stamped horizontal slats with a shadow under each
- palette: punched sheet #d2d3cf with hole interior #101112 and hole rim highlight #f4f5f2 (lower) / shadow #9b9c98 (upper); sparkle silver #c9ccd2 / #e8ebf0 with black #1b1b1c and a blue cast #9aa3b3; basketweave black #1c1a18 and brown #3d2f24 with highlight #5a4a3a; honeycomb #232426 with #4a4c50 edges; expanded #7c7f82 with #b8bbbe strand highlights and #0f1011 diamonds; louvre #8a8c8e with slot shadow #1e2022 and lip #c4c6c8
- typeface: none
- the tells:
  1. punched: perfect round holes in a perfect square grid — each hole's rim has a shadow at the top and a light at the bottom (the sheet has thickness), and whatever is behind shows dark
  2. sparkle: the crossings of silver threads glint — a scatter of tiny bright points on a grey-blue weave, black threads making a faint diagonal
  3. basketweave: a coarse over-under structure at 12 px, black over brown, with real depth (a shadow under each over-strand)
  4. honeycomb: a hex mesh with dark interiors — the hexes are regular and the mesh is black
  5. expanded: every strand is twisted, so the diamonds have one bright edge and one dark, and the pattern is slightly irregular
  6. louvre: each slat has a bright top lip and a hard shadow into the slot beneath; nothing shows through
  7. all of them read as *surfaces with holes*: the `<slot>` content behind (a speaker cone, a dark cavity, a fan) shows through where there are holes
- motion: none; a `fan` attribute behind the punched or expanded grille spins a dark blur at 2 rev/s
- states to show: punched over a dark cavity; sparkle over a speaker cone; basketweave; expanded with a fan behind
- priority: C
